sources.supports: Each Google Account includes up to 15 GB shared across Gmail, Drive and Photos; 'Gmail messages and attachments, which includes your Spam and Trash folders' count; Drive files, Photos, Android and WhatsApp backups count; large deletions normally take up to 48–72 hours to update.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 via curl (title 'How your Google storage works - Google One Help'). Quota sentence, 'What counts' list and 48–72 hour FAQ answer confirmed verbatim. The article says 'up to 15 GB on a standard account', matching 'up to 15 GB'.

sources.supports: Trash and Spam count against the storage limit until permanently cleared; allow up to 48–72 hours; Gmail search example has:attachment larger:10M; backups and hidden app data under other storage.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 via curl (title 'Manage your storage in Drive, Gmail & Photos'). Confirmed 'Until you permanently clear items in these folders, they count against your storage limit' and the has:attachment larger:10M example.

sources.supports: Operators in:anywhere ('This includes emails in Spam and Trash'), in:archive, category:, label:, from:me, has:attachment, larger:; negative-operator/conversation caveat (Gmail identifies matching messages first).
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 via curl (title 'Refine searches in Gmail - Computer'). Each operator used in the article appears in the table. in:sent and in:spam are NOT in the table, so the article uses the Sent/Spam folders and from:me instead. The combinations (in:anywhere larger:10M, in:archive larger:10M, from:me has:attachment larger:10M) rely on the page's general statement that operators can be combined; they were not run live.

sources.supports: Archived messages no longer appear in the inbox but can be found under All mail; in:archive search; replies return archived conversations to the inbox.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 via curl (title 'Archive Gmail messages - Computer'). Confirmed.

sources.supports: Labels are different from folders; 'When you delete an email, it's removed from every label and your inbox.'
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 via curl (title 'Create & manage labels in Gmail - Computer'). Quoted sentence confirmed. The article's 'a label is a tag, not a copy' is an inference from this sentence and 'Labels are different from folders'; Google does not state storage accounting per label explicitly.

sources.supports: Default inbox type sorts mail into Primary, Social, Promotions, Updates and Forums; category: search; 'Archived emails don't appear in categories'.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 via curl (title 'Organize your emails into categories - Computer'). Confirmed category list and search syntax.

sources.supports: Deleted messages move to Trash; recoverable up to 30 days; Empty Trash now; select-all banner extends selection beyond the current page.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 via curl (title 'Delete messages in Gmail - Computer'). Confirmed.

serp_review.query: why is gmail storage full when my inbox is empty
serp_review.observation: Standard web search returned getinboxzero.com (exact-intent title), clean.email, picbackman x2, dev.to, a codingblocks forum thread, a Mozilla support thread, a Google accounts community thread and getmailbird. Common points: Trash/Spam, archived mail, Drive/Photos shared quota, update lag (one unsourced 'up to seven days'), wrong account. Result summaries did not show category tabs as a hiding place, the label-is-not-a-copy point, sent attachments, or Google-documented operators per location.
serp_review.limitation: One standard US web search summary; result pages were not opened individually. Not a Google ranking capture.

information_gain: A location map of every place Gmail mail can sit outside the inbox view (category tabs, archive/All Mail, labels, Sent, Spam, Trash, outside Gmail), each paired with a Google-documented way to check it, plus the 'label is a tag, not a copy' clarification sourced to the labels help page, and a size-first search order using in:anywhere (documented as including Spam and Trash). Top results list generic causes but did not show tabs, label copies or per-location operators. Avoids the undocumented in:sent/in:spam operators other pages use.
overlap_check: Hub gmail-mailbox-full-cant-receive-emails covers delivery failure; gmail-archive-vs-delete covers the archive decision (linked, not repeated). Unpublished sibling drafts gmail-empty-trash-storage-still-full and gmail-storage-not-updating-after-deleting start from a deletion the reader already made; this draft starts from the misconception that an empty inbox means an empty mailbox. Residual overlap: all three mention Spam/Trash counting and 48–72 hours, and pending topics gmail-storage-full-archive-does-not-help and gmail-spam-trash-storage-quota overlap the archive and Spam/Trash rows. The archive section here is two sentences and routes to the existing guide. A reviewer should confirm the cluster does not need consolidation before publishing more than one of these.
limitations: Source and documentation review only. No live Gmail mailbox test was run; the combined searches were not executed and no screenshots exist.
The 'label is not a copy / does not change storage' framing is inferred from Gmail's labels help ('removed from every label'), not a direct Google storage statement.
The storage page's per-service breakdown is described generically; its exact UI was not checked live.
The 48–72 hour update timing is Google's 'normally' figure, not a guarantee.
Covers personal accounts in Gmail on a computer; mobile app views and Workspace admin quotas are out of scope.
review_needed: An independent substantive reviewer should re-read the seven Google pages claim by claim, ideally run the three combined searches in a test mailbox, decide the overlap with the two sibling storage drafts and the archive/spam pending topics, and only then promote a record into scripts/content-records.json with real identity, verified_on and post_sha256.
